html:
Sputnik 1 was the first artificial satellite. The Soviet Union launched it on 4 October 1957 from the test range that became the Baikonur Cosmodrome, in the Kazakh steppe, and with it began the space age.

It was a polished metal ball 58 centimetres across, with four long radio antennas. It sent a simple beeping signal for three weeks, until its batteries died, and anyone with a radio receiver could hear it. It fell back and burned up in January 1958.

It was launched on an R-7 rocket, the world's first intercontinental ballistic missile, designed by the team of Sergei Korolev. That was the frightening part for the West: a rocket that could put a satellite in orbit could also reach America with a nuclear warhead.

The launch caught the United States by surprise and set off the Sputnik crisis:

  • The Space Race began; the United States launched its own first satellite in January 1958.
  • The United States created NASA in 1958.
  • Congress poured money into science and engineering education.

Scientists also learned from it. Its slowing orbit showed the density of the upper atmosphere, and its radio signals gave data on the ionosphere. It was launched during the International Geophysical Year.

Four years later Yuri Gagarin flew from the same launch site to become the first human in space.
sum: Sputnik 1 was the first artificial satellite. The Soviet Union launched it on 4 October 1957 from the test range that became the Baikonur Cosmodrome, in the Kazakh steppe, and with it began the space age.
